slides.heading: Lists of Numbers
slides.body: Lists of Numbers is part of Lists and Mutable Sequences. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Lists of Numbers
slides.body: Lists of numbers can be combined with loops or built-in functions to calculate totals and averages.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A list of numbers is like a grade sheet where each score can contribute to a final result.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Lists use square brackets, zero-based indexes, and can be changed after creation.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a list of three scores and print their total using sum().

coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
